case.description: Build a bounded review workflow for deciding whether a synthetic text classifier's proposed update deserves a further evaluation round. The task is to support that decision from supplied results and limited adjudication, without declaring deployment readiness.
case.valued_outcome: Produce a reproducible advance, reject or unresolved decision under the supplied acceptance rule, identify affected slices, and account for every adjudication used.
hard_constraints: Use only supplied records and labels; no outside examples.
Apply the stated acceptance rule without changing thresholds.
At most sixteen disputed labels may be adjudicated.
Report uncertainty when the adjudication limit prevents a supported decision.
resources: Eighty synthetic examples with baseline and candidate predictions, provisional labels and one of four slice identifiers.
A supplied rule: advance only if total correct predictions improve by at least four and no slice loses more than two.
A sealed adjudication table for twenty-four flagged labels, accessible one selected row at a time.
Spreadsheet or local script environment and seventy minutes of analyst time.
observations: Against provisional labels, the candidate gains six correct predictions overall.
One slice loses two and contains nine flagged labels.
Awkward observation: the slice with the largest apparent improvement also contains the most disagreements between the two supplied provisional annotators.

openings.claim: Replace dependence on provisional confusion counts with a decision certificate over possible correctness contributions of unadjudicated flagged records. This may distinguish acceptance-rule uncertainty from annotation disagreement.
openings.delta: Changed dependency/carrier: the decision uses per-record candidate-minus-baseline correctness envelopes and slice envelopes. Equal predictions contribute zero regardless of label. For differing predictions, enumerate contributions from supplied label possibilities; where possibilities are unspecified, retain the conservative range [-1,1]. Select accessible flagged records whose possible revelations most affect certification, using recorded deterministic ties. Log withheld attempts and retain their uncertainty.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: adjudicate the largest provisional-annotator disagreements first, then recount. The envelope workflow could reach a supported decision with fewer revealed labels when disagreement-heavy records have little prediction influence. If both orders expose the same decisive records, no advantage is predicted. This is an unmeasured hypothesis.
openings.probe: On matched copies, run envelope-directed selection versus disagreement-first selection, each within seventy minutes and sixteen adjudications. Freeze advance/reject/unresolved reports before opening the full-label key. Record all selections, withheld attempts, reveals, time, affected slices, certificate bounds and key agreement. Advance only when every remaining feasible assignment meets total gain >=4 and each slice gain >=-2; reject only when none can meet both; otherwise unresolved. Compare correct supported decisions and adjudications consumed. A stop cap alone is not evidence of usefulness.
assumptions: The supplied records permit paired prediction contributions and slice grouping; availability must be checked without adding records.
Bounds cover every possible adjudicated label, including labels outside provisional alternatives.

Defeat conditions: withheld or excess pivotal rows leave the envelope crossing acceptance boundaries; then report unresolved. Loose bounds or computation exceeding analyst capacity can erase any benefit.
Successful certificates concern a further evaluation round only.

openings.claim: Use conservative decision bounds to direct adjudication and permit advance or reject only when every remaining label assignment supports that decision.
openings.delta: Replace dependence on provisional aggregate gains with a script or spreadsheet carrying per-record candidate-minus-baseline correctness contributions and slice bounds. Equal predictions contribute zero; unadjudicated flagged rows with differing predictions conservatively contribute between minus one and plus one. Adjudications fix contributions. Log selected identifiers, selection reasons, responses, unavailable attempts, allowance use and elapsed time.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, a fixed slice-stratified sixteen-row review using corrected point totals, bounds should prevent unsupported threshold decisions when residual label uncertainty could reverse them. They need not produce more resolved decisions or require fewer adjudications.
openings.probe: Run both workflows on matched copies, with identical preselected withheld rows. Select accessible rows whose possible contributions can change the total threshold of four or a slice threshold of minus two; use record-ID tie breaks. Advance when the total lower bound is at least four and every slice lower bound is at least minus two. Reject when the total upper bound is below four or any slice upper bound is below minus two. Otherwise continue within sixteen successful adjudications and seventy minutes, then report unresolved with affected slices and remaining bounds. Unavailable attempts consume no allowance and remain logged. Freeze both reports before opening the full-label key; compare decisions, residual uncertainty, adjudications and time.
assumptions: Unflagged supplied labels remain fixed for this review; if their status is also disputed, these bounds cannot certify a decision.
The local environment must implement and verify conservative bounds within seventy minutes; otherwise report unresolved.

The rival is defeated only by demonstrated unsupported decisions or comparable certainty at greater cost. If both remain unresolved, no advantage is established. Withheld or numerous pivotal rows may prevent resolution.

artifact.assessment: This is a bounded review probe, not deployment evidence. Apparent improvement remains provisional until the unchanged acceptance rule is supported; disagreement alone does not establish label error.

openings.delta: Change the decision dependency from completed adjudication counts to worst-case certificates. Carry paired candidate-minus-baseline correctness intervals in the confusion table, grouped by slice. Unresolved differing predictions contribute conservatively from minus one to plus one; agreeing predictions contribute zero. Select an accessible flagged row whose possible adjudication most reduces uncertainty at a threatened acceptance boundary, with deterministic record-ID tie-breaking.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: adjudicate the sixteen highest-disagreement rows before applying ordinary counts. The certificate workflow may reach a supported verdict with fewer adjudications when disagreements are concentrated on prediction agreements or harmless margins. If disagreement instead coincides with decisive rows, the rival may match or outperform it. Differing observations are adjudications to a supported verdict, unresolved frequency, and agreement with the sealed decision key.
openings.probe: On the two matched copies, run certificate selection and the rival within seventy minutes and each sixteen-row allowance. Preselect the same four withheld rows. Log selections, reasons, results, unsuccessful access and elapsed time; unsuccessful access spends no allowance. Advance only when the total lower bound is at least four and every slice lower bound is at least minus two. Reject only when the total upper bound is below four or a slice upper bound is below minus two. Otherwise continue or report unresolved at the capacity limit. Freeze both reports before opening the full-label key.
assumptions: Individual supplied records support reproducible paired correctness calculations; no new labels or examples are introduced.

The actual influence distribution is unknown. Withheld pivotal rows or more than sixteen necessary resolutions defeat early certification; wide conservative bounds can leave an otherwise decidable case unresolved.
The bounded experiment tests enabling feasibility, not deployment readiness or reliable improvement.
